source.title: GD over Diagonal Linear Networks: Implicit Regularisation, Large Stepsizes and Edge of Stability
source.authors: Mathieu Even; Scott Pesme; Epfl Suriya Gunasekar; Nicolas Flammarion

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figures are garbled in extraction, but the main text and result descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent on synthetic sparse regression and reports how stepsizes and minibatch size affect recovery and test loss. It does not test the claim versions' natural-label classification settings or their specified interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports sparse-recovery results for a diagonal linear network, not natural-label generalization or the training-to-test error gap. It also discusses prior work on batch size and generalization; those cited findings are not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study reports implicit bias and sparse recovery in diagonal linear networks, but tests none of V1–V8. Its batch comparisons use solutions at convergence rather than fixed epoch budgets (V5), and its Hessian measures are neither magnitude-aware perturbation measures nor rankings of generalization gaps (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove convergence under stated stepsize conditions and characterize solutions through trajectory-dependent implicit regularization. Their centered sparse-regression results show that large stepsizes benefit SGD but can impair GD recovery; edge-of-stability explanations are heuristic, and uncentered inputs can change GD's behavior.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic noiseless sparse regression with a two-layer diagonal linear network; the study analyzes GD and minibatch SGD rather than the listed natural-label classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Stepsize, minibatch size, and centered versus uncentered inputs change the reported recovery behavior; GD and SGD respond differently to large stepsizes on centered data.

fits_no_version.finding: For centered Gaussian sparse regression, increasing stepsize improves SGD recovery but worsens GD recovery; the gain vector is relatively homogeneous for SGD and disproportionately penalizes sparse-support coordinates for GD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stepsize and stochasticity alter sparse recovery through the scale and coordinate structure of implicit regularization in diagonal linear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing stepsize decreases GD's maximum Hessian eigenvalue despite worsening recovery, whereas SGD's Hessian trace decreases alongside improving recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different Hessian notions of flatness can accompany different sparse-recovery outcomes in diagonal linear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: With Gaussian inputs shifted by μ=5 in every coordinate, GD and SGD show similar recovery behavior, and large stepsizes help recover the sparse solution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input centering and the direction of the input mean affect how large stepsizes influence sparse recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: At the edge of stability, GD's sparse-support coordinates oscillate and drift toward zero; SGD fluctuates across coordinates and recovers the sparse solution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coordinate-specific oscillations distinguish GD and SGD recovery at the edge of stability in diagonal linear networks.

record.problems: The experiments use a simplified diagonal linear network and synthetic noiseless sparse regression rather than natural-label classification. Several findings are figure-only in the supplied extraction, so numeric values and uncertainty cannot be recovered. The edge-of-stability discussion is explicitly heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result on the listed versions was identified. Cited results about other studies' models and generalization are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting together with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including recovery interventions.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove them.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed version; this does not deny the explicitly reported sparse-recovery effects. Citations to original generalization studies and the resemblance of gain scaling to a linear learning-rate scaling rule do not constitute tests of those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the listed classification models.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers and held-out performance under limited tuning.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a measure of the training-to-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer diagonal linear network, GD
rows.operation_detail: Varied constant stepsize in noiseless sparse regression; measured test loss relative to the minimum ℓ1-norm interpolator.
rows.note: The text states that increasing stepsize deteriorates GD's generalization properties; figure values are not recoverable as numbers.
rows.check: Figure 1 explicitly reports worsening recovery with increasing GD stepsize, but this does not measure any listed version; partial is inapplicable.

rows.note: The text states that increasing stepsize improves SGD's generalization properties; figure values are not recoverable as numbers.
rows.check: Figure 1 explicitly reports improving recovery with increasing SGD stepsize, but this does not measure any listed version; partial is inapplicable.

rows.subject: 2-layer diagonal linear network, GD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test loss across stepsizes, including near the largest convergent stepsize.
rows.note: The authors state that large stepsizes can prevent recovery of the sparse interpolator for GD.
rows.check: Figure 2 left measures the scale of Gainγ, not test loss. As a test-loss row this duplicates R1; either remove it or change its measure to gain magnitude approaching the convergence threshold.
